mechanism_comparison.standard_core: Reducing N=kpN_prev+1-b modulo p forces b to occupy one residue class modulo p. A sharp interval containing exactly k such representatives writes that class uniquely as b=1+pr; division by p leaves the congruence p^(k-1) divides kN_prev-r.
mechanism_comparison.why_not_Hensel: Hensel lifting concerns lifting roots of polynomial congruences under derivative hypotheses. Here there is no iterative root-lifting problem: the theorem is a direct quotient-remainder decomposition of one linear congruence.
mechanism_comparison.why_not_LTE: The lifting-the-exponent lemma evaluates p-adic valuations of expressions such as x^n-y^n. The current result merely factors one forced p after selecting a residue slot.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: For k=2, the sharp carry range leaves exactly b=1 and b=1+p, producing the two displayed predecessor congruences. The Lean consumer then connects cofinal failure of both branches to the already established rational-denominator obstruction for the literal factorial-gap series.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: The theorem classifies square hits; it provides no estimate, distribution law, or proof that either branch fails cofinally.
